answer.rationale: Write-path p99 has climbed gradually for 90 minutes during daily settlement peak, which fits primary saturation under heavy writes better than an instant deploy cliff. Objective forbids shedding customer writes, so circuit breaking is rejected despite the partner-outage memory. Replica routing previously helped only when dashboard reads were on the primary, which is not in evidence. No regional signal for failover. Adding capacity is the intervention that keeps accepting writes while absorbing the peak; rollback stays a live alternative if archive review of the day-18 incident shows a performance regression rather than errors, and if day-47 capacity work was only effective when pre-provisioned. Settlement value is on the write path, so any change is treated as downstream-value-risky. Cause remains ambiguous (release vs peak vs both).
